name: Carousel
description: A section that displays items sequentially, typically one slide at a time, with controls for navigating between slides and optionally controlling automatic rotation.

keyboard_interactions.action: Moves focus through interactive elements in the carousel
Moves focus to previous interactive element in the carousel

roles.description: Identifies the carousel as a landmark
Identifies each slide as a group
Groups the tab elements for slide selection
Used instead of group for tabbed variant

required_attributes.description: Provides accessible name for the carousel

optional_attributes.description: Set to 'polite' when not auto-rotating; 'off' during auto-rotation
Set to false so only changed content is announced
true on the currently displayed slide's picker control

notes: Auto-rotation requires a visible, keyboard-reachable pause control (RAWeb 13.8). This is not a nicety — a rotating carousel with no pause is a straight failure.
Auto-rotation must pause on hover AND on focus within the carousel, or a keyboard user tabbing through the slides has the content move out from under them.
Prefer not auto-rotating at all. It is the single easiest way to pass 13.8.
Off-screen slides must be `hidden` or inert — translating them off-screen leaves every slide's links in the tab order at once (RAWeb 10.8).
aria-live='polite' goes on the slide CONTAINER and is only meaningful while paused. During auto-rotation it would announce endlessly; set it to 'off' while rotating.
aria-roledescription='carousel' renames the region for screen readers. It does NOT replace an accessible name — you still need aria-label.
The tabs variant (slide picker dots as role='tab') is valid, but only if the dots really behave like tabs — see patterns/tabs.md.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion: do not auto-rotate at all when it is set.

raweb_criteria.reason: THE criterion for this pattern. Auto-rotation is moving content: the user MUST be able to pause, stop or hide it. A carousel that rotates with no pause control fails outright.
Controls and the rotation state must be exposed; aria-roledescription='carousel' names the widget.
Previous/next/pause must all be reachable and operable by keyboard.
Slide changes are status messages: aria-live on the slide container announces them, but ONLY while rotation is paused.
Focus must be visible on the controls, which usually sit over busy imagery.
Off-screen slides must be hidden from assistive technologies, not merely translated out of view.
